jobs.title: Research Assistant/Associate I
jobs.description:
Programmable Medicine, a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company located in Redwood City, is seeking

a Research Associate/Lab Manager for the Chemistry Department. Programmable Medicine is focused on developing novel nanomedicines, HD therapeutics (HDTs), to treat unmet medical needs in ophthalmology, neurology, inflammatory diseases, and neuro-oncology. Our HD platform builds therapeutics that are selectively taken up only by inflamed tissues, allowing us to treat diseases with unprecedented precision.

We are seeking an individual who is motivated to learn and has a basic understanding and familiarity with laboratory equipment and processes. The responsibilities of this position include performing standard chemical reactions and analysis, helping to purchase/maintain laboratory supplies/inventories, equipment maintenance , and ensuring compliance with laboratory safety and compliance.

To thrive in this role, a person should enjoy a small company environment where you will work on a variety of tasks, from playing a hands on role in the lab to maintaining inventories and managing laboratory supplies. Individuals who are ambitious and demonstrate a willingness to learn will have the opportunity to develop as a researcher and a contributor to our scientific efforts over time. This person should be proactive in finding ways to streamline laboratory function and enable the team to achieve higher productivity. A person who is driven by enhancing productivity through daily efforts to streamline processes will be highly appreciated!

**Duties and Responsibilities - Essential Functions**

* Perform basic chemical synthesis and analysis – Work with the chemistry team to learn our platform and contribute to a novel approach for developing therapeutics
* Instrument maintenance and development – work with vendors and technicians to install, enhance, maintain, and learn new techniques on current and future equipment
* Assist Scientists with compound management – Consolidate, standardize, dispense, track, store
* Coordinate the purchase of routine chemical and consumables in support of the laboratory operations, organize laboratory materials to ensure all staff are able to find what they need
* Work with our safety consultant to ensure laboratory compliance and proper waste management.
* Other tasks may include light management of chemistry group software licenses, organizing the stockroom, and other roles as needed.

**Job Requirements**

* Bachelor Degree in a related scientific discipline (preferable chemistry) with 0-2 years of relevant experience. New college graduates must have completed at least one internship playing a hands-on role in a laboratory or part-time work, during undergraduate degree, working in a laboratory setting.
* Demonstrated experience and a passion for organizing and maintaining a lab
* Solid presentation, writing, and communication skills along with problem solving and mathematical skills
* Forward-thinking and creative with high ethical standards and a strong work ethic
* Strategic thinker with good judgment and strong operational focus
* Well organized and self-directed
* Must be able to work on-site five full days per week at our Redwood City Laboratory 5 days per week

**What We Can Offer You**

This is a unique opportunity to join a team focused on the development of a new class of precision

medicines that selectively treat diseased cells in regions of inflammation. By making precision medicine

even more precise, our nanomedicine technology has the potential to change the standard of care across

ophthalmology, neurology, inflammatory diseases and neuro-oncology. You will have the opportunity to

learn new skills and gain a better understanding of the cutting-edge technology.

We have a comprehensive total compensation package including fully paid medical, dental and vision

benefits for you and your family. We want all of our employees to have the opportunity to become

shareholders and offer new hire stock options. The Company also offers participation in the annual bonus program. The base salary for this position is $65,000 – $80,000 per year. We consider various factors when determining the base compensation, including market survey data, experience, qualifications, and geographic location, which means that the actual compensation may vary.

jobs.title: Staff Research Associate 2 (9612C), Molecular & Cell Biology - #89397
jobs.description:
Staff Research Associate 2 (9612C), Molecular & Cell Biology - #89397 About Berkeley
  
  
At the University of California, Berkeley , we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation - driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.
  
  
At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth . We actively support professional development by providing all full-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.
  
  
We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan , which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.
  
  
Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride .
  
  
Departmental Overview
  
  
The Department of Molecular and Cell Biology at UC Berkeley is recognized nationally and internationally for excellence. The teaching and research activities of the Department of Molecular and Cell Biology (MCB) concern the molecular structures and processes of cellular life and their roles in the function, reproduction, and development of living organisms. The types of living organisms from which the departmental faculty draws its working materials range from viruses and microbes through plants, roundworms, annelids, arthropods, and mollusks to fish, amphibia, and mammals.
  
  
The Hockemeyer Lab work to establish reliable models of human diseases using genetically engineered human and stem cell and mouse models and functional genomics screening approaches. We are particularly interested in developing rigorous genetic approaches to study human disease, development and cell biology where conventional animal models or tissue culture systems do not adequately recapitulate human biology.
  
  
Position Summary
  
  
This Staff Research Associate 2 provides a variety of support and research functions within the lab for a 2-year project. This position assists lab members with molecular biology and tissue culture techniques, including the culture and maintenance of pluripotent stem cell cultures (hPSCs). The Staff Research Associate 2 supports a large-scale hPSCs genome engineering workflow involving genome editing, project tracking, and quality control. Additionally, this position works on various research projects involving the planning, design, and conduct of experiments under the supervision of the PI, while assisting with general lab operations, safety compliance, and supply management.
  
  
Application Review Date
  
  
**The First Review Date for this job is:** October 23, 2026. For full consideration, please apply on or before the first review date.
  
  
Responsibilities
  
  
Stem Cell Culture and Genome Engineering - 30%
  
  
Cultures and maintains the pluripotent stem cell cultures (hPSCs) which includes the passaging of stem cell clones, isolation of genomic DNA and genotyping cells by PCR and sequencing. Support a large-scale hPSCs genome engineering workflow that involves genome editing, project tracking, quality control of reagents and materials, and report writing.
  
  
Molecular Biology and Tissue Culture Support - 25%
  
  
Standard molecular biology and tissue culture techniques. Assists lab members with the maintenance and characterization of human stem cell cultures and genotyping of stem cells which entails the isolation of DNA from human stem cells, amplifying DNA by PCR and preparing samples for sequence analysis. This genotyping will require daily record keeping in laboratory notebook to record the samples analyzed and the attendance at weekly lab meetings to understand the basic objectives of the research project.
  
  
Research Project Support - 25%
  
  
Assists with research projects including optimizing and testing tissue culture and molecular biology protocols such as molecular cloning, stem cell differentiation and library screening. This will be done with the guidance of the PI and other lab members.
  
Plans and designs the experiments discussing the outline of the experiment/ protocol with the PI, conducting the experiments, analyzing results and interpreting data under the supervision of the PI. Troubleshoots experiments which include PCR and genotyping.
  
  
Safety and Protocol Compliance - 10%
  
  
Assisting with protocol renewals and safety inspections.
  
  
Lab Support Operations - 10%
  
  
Lab support duties including autoclaving waste and ordering and restocking supplies.
  
  
Required Qualifications
  
  
Experience with sterile tissue culture techniques, PCR, basic lab maintenance duties, excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.
  
Experience with molecular biology techniques, plasmid handling and molecular cloning.
  
Experience with human pluripotent stem cell culturing, genome engineering with CRISPR, as well as the library prep and data analysis of next generation sequencing (NGS).
  
Knowledge of lab safety procedures, capability to design and conduct experiments and analyze data.
  
  
Preferred Qualifications
  
  
Master's degree in the life sciences, preferably Biology, Molecular and Cell Biology, Biochemistry. (Preferred)
  
  
Education / Training
  
  
Bachelor's degree in the life sciences, preferably Biology, Molecular and Cell Biology, Biochemistry.
  
1-year (cumulative) experience working in a biology research lab.
  
  
Salary & Benefits
  
  
For information on the comprehensive benefits package offered by the University, please visit the University of C
